author: fastdude
text: On FastH3's contract graph the dense attention backend never executes: switching ModelAttentionBackend from kitchen int8 to bf16 gives bit-identical final latents on look_anchor and slapstick. The backend serves only dense_blocks, out-of-window steps and sequences under min_tokens, and this graph has none, so the fused VSA kernel does all the attention. Sage vs kitchen is moot here.

author: fastdude
text: The kitchen upgrade to 0.2.35+sol.863e953.up.c8c7825 (upstream #207/#208) leaves our renders bit-identical (20 of 20 saved latents, PDD8 exact, FlashGen and PDD strength arms) and makes sampling 0.3-1.1% faster: same arithmetic, new scheduling on the int8 dense tail. It also shows PDD8 exact and FlashGen reproduce bit for bit across server processes.

author: fastdude
text: #34: finishing PDD8 from sigma 0.8 with FlashGen on blocks 34-49 matches the full-FlashGen finish. Haze is within 0.002 between the two finishers on noodle_bar, radio_drama, courtroom_verdict and subway_chase, and the full finish adds no haze over PDD8 in the first place, so the late-only finisher has nothing to remove. Both lift highlights (not on noodle_bar) and detail alike. Full FlashGen stays the finisher; FT1's 'early blocks carry the haze' holds for FlashGen from noise, not for a late finish.
basis: 1 seed, 7 new renders plus 5 existing, measured, not judged by eye

author: fastdude
scope: PDD8 finishes from sigma 0.8, seven t2v scenes and one i2v
text: The finisher grid: finishing PDD8 from 0.8 with full FlashGen or with FlashGen's late blocks gives near-identical clips on all seven t2v scenes (#34 holds). Either lifts PDD8's highlights where they are dim (radio_drama, courtroom, subway, subway_chase_short, i2v) and raises detail everywhere. The base finish (#37) barely moves PDD8's tone or detail and does not repair its highlights, though it adds some motion detail.
basis: 1 seed, 24 renders plus existing rows, measured, not judged

author: fastdude
scope: FlashGen alone, full against blocks 34-49, five scenes at 124 frames
text: #46 on measures: FlashGen on its late blocks alone has less haze on three of five scenes and more on two (on spec_typical, much hazier with half the detail), and less contrast on four. FT1's 'about half the haze' (two scenes at 345 frames) does not generalise. A control re-render reproduced the old full-FlashGen row bit for bit across the Sol redesign and kitchen move. Adherence, #46's question, awaits the owner's eye.
basis: 1 seed, 6 new renders plus existing rows, measured, not judged

author: fastdude
text: Telemetry (#39): the card peaks at 24.3-24.5 GB on every render; the DiT stays about 90% resident with the rest streamed every forward (74-168 GiB PCIe on 345-frame renders); the text encoder loads and evicts per new prompt (8.5-10 s, 22-31 GiB PCIe) and costs nothing on a repeated prompt. About 19.5 GB of disk reads per new-prompt render suggest page-cache eviction, with a CPU sweep running alongside.

author: vaedude
text: The follow-up's radio_drama and radio_drama_v2 are one configuration rendered twice about two hours apart (same prompt_sha256, seed, length, graph, LoRAs, VAE, sampler, schedule, shift, attention), not v1 against v2. Neither was a cache hit, and their saved final latents are bit-identical, video and audio, on PDD8, FlashGen and FastH3. PDD8 and FlashGen span 0.155.0 to 0.156.0; FastH3 spans two commits inside 0.156.0. Rendering is deterministic at this seed across those code changes.

author: vaedude
text: The owner's 'FlashGen audio is louder than PDD' on radio_drama is measured: integrated loudness -15.1 LUFS (FlashGen) and -14.4 (FastH3) against -24.5 (PDD8), about 9 LU. Across 13 scenes the medians are close (FlashGen -22.4, FastH3 -22.2, PDD -23.4), so the gap is this scene's, not a FlashGen trait; PDD8 is the quietest by median.
